text:
emily: Quick heads-up — I finished the spike on 'slice cohesion' (observability + ingest). Putting the summary here for a design-week sync.
raj: link: https://go/redwood/spikes/slice-cohesion (tmp doc) — thanks emily, will read.
chris: TL;DR?
emily: TL;DR: extracting the telemetry ingest path into a slim sidecar buys deploy isolation and simpler scaling, but adds an RPC hop for hotpath traces. Tradeoffs below.
rachel: Nice. main worry is contract drift over time. We need a versioned contract + graceful fallback story before cutting traffic.
emily: Agreed. Proposal: start with a strict v1 contract, implement a compatibility shim in the monolith that accepts v1+v1-compat, and ship a canary route with 5% traffic.
chris: Can you paste the proposed surface?
emily: Sure — minimal interface we tested: 
```json
{
  "proto": "rwb.telemetry.v1.Ingest",
  "methods": ["BatchEvents", "StreamSpans"],
  "auth": "mtls",
  "backpressure": "token-bucket"
}
```
raj: Nice. Important: how do we handle high-cardinality attributes that blow up RPC size?
emily: We observed two failure modes in the spike: 1) oversized batches -> OOM on sidecar, 2) tail latency due to sync flush. Mitigations: enforce batch size cap + async flush + per-tenant batching window.
jordan: For rollback, can we route directly to existing telemetry pipeline if the sidecar is unhealthy?
emily: Yes — routing policy idea: prefer sidecar; if p99 > 200ms or errors > 1% over 1m, fallback to monolith ingest (no schema evolution until fixed). We'll bake that into the control plane.
dario-bot: CI: modular-spike-tests — 1 failing test (batch-size-enforcement) on linux-amd64. @emily assigned.
chris: Cost note: sidecars increase infra count (N more pods). Rough calc from spike: +12% infra CPU; but tokenized cost decreases because we can batch better, so per-ingest unit cost down ~8%. Net ~+4% until we tune.
raj: That delta is OK if SLOs stay tight. We need an SLA runbook for slower p99 degradation scenarios.
emily: We'll add a stability-anchor plan: 
- contract minor-versioning (v1, v1.1 compatibility shims)
- canary + measured dashboards (p50/p95/p99, error %, cost delta)
- rollback flow -> immediate route-shift to monolith + alert for owners
- gating: require perf regression <= 7% p99 and error <= 0.5% in canary to progress

rachel: Love the gating. Also add an automated regression test that replays 10k sampled traces to validate interface correctness.
emily: Good call. I'll put that in the RFC.
chris: Implementation notes: keep hot cache (prefix/KV) in the sidecar to avoid RTT for common prefixes. If that gets expensive, we can move to an in-host shared-memory cache later.
jordan: Ops question: who owns rollout and rollback?
emily: Owners: emily (design + rollout), chris (runtime + perf), raj (stability + SLA). Add oncall rotation for the first 6 weeks.
raj: Ping @platform-eng for gate automation (canary -> promote).
emily: Next steps: update RFC with the contract snippet, add regression harness, schedule design review Tue 10am. @chris @raj @rachel please confirm availability.
rachel: :thumbsup: I'll be there.
chris: I can make Tue 10am.
jordan: +1
emily: Great — I'll send calendar invite and a short pre-read. Thanks all.
